This project brought us closer as a family, working together toward a common goal.
summary:
DELTA V PROJECT: Autonomous Offline-First Navigation & Life Support for MarsDelta V Project is an offline-first, dual-mode Progressive Web App (PWA) designed to ensure astronaut survival and mission success from Martian Landing Zones to future bases. Hosted on Netlify, the app bypasses internet dependency by delivering 100% offline navigation powered solely by local device GPS.

From Simulation to Arcadia Planitia: Using Spaceflight Simulator and NASA/USGS datasets (terrain, subsurface ice, radiation), we identified Arcadia Planitia as the optimal landing and base site.

Dual-Mode Survival Tech: Built with AI-assisted code, the app operates for both EVA astronauts and Rovers, featuring custom interfaces for AR helmet HUDs, forearm tablets, and rover consoles.

Critical Life-Support & Mapping: It actively monitors vital resources ($O_2$, water, battery) against topographic risks (slopes), while allowing crews to log waypoints, resources, and hazards in real time.

The Impact: Delta V secures human life where communications fail. Easily adaptable to Lunar Artemis missions and Earth-based search-and-rescue in disaster zones, it turns hostile terrain into a life-saving, shared planetary database.

👉 Launch live PWA: https://deltavproject.netlify.app
details:
THE SOLUTION: DELTA V PROJECT (Título sugerido para la Slide)

An offline-first navigation and life-support platform for human Martian exploration (Subtítulo)

  • The Challenge: To secure human movement, scouting, and survival on Mars from day one—navigating and exploring unfamiliar terrain with no real-time internet connection or external infrastructure.
  • How the App Resolves It (Offline-First GIS & GPS): Using a Progressive Web App (PWA) hosted on Netlify, we bypass traditional connectivity barriers to offer 100% offline navigation in the field, relying purely on localized device GPS. By pre-integrating NASA and USGS datasets, the app allows astronauts and rovers to safely move across Arcadia Planitia without active network connections.
    • Interactive Dual-Mode (EVA & Rover): Real-time telemetries tailored to the astronaut's AR helmet visor, forearm tablet, and the rover’s cockpit.
    • Adaptive Life Support Tracking: A predictive algorithm that continuously calculates and forecasts survival resources ($O_2$ depletion, cooling water, and battery life) against real terrain slope risks.
    • Dynamic Mapping: Active tracking and marking of waypoints, resources (such as subsurface ice/water), and environmental hazards directly in the field.
  • Our Mission Success: We empower crews to turn a hostile, isolated landscape into an assessable, traversable map—ensuring that every mission beyond the Landing Zone is not just viable, but survivable.

PROJECT IMPACT (Slide Title)

  • 👩‍🚀 Human Survival & Mission Safety (Zero-Connectivity Autonomy):
    Eliminates reliance on Earth-based communications during critical EVAs, reducing navigation errors and preventing life-support depletion ($O_2$, water, battery) in unfamiliar Martian terrain.
  • 🔬 Accelerated Scientific Discovery:
    Turns every astronaut and rover expedition into a live geological survey—logging subsurface ice, minerals, and hazards in real time to build a shared, growing planetary database.
    • Space: Adaptable to the Moon (Artemis missions) and future planetary bodies simply by swapping orbital datasets.
    • Earth: Immediately applicable in disaster zones, search-and-rescue operations, and remote expeditions where cellular networks and internet infrastructure fail.

Project Development Timeline

  • 1. Define, Simulate & Site Selection (The Starting Point)
    • Used Spaceflight Simulator and comprehensive data analysis to evaluate optimal sites, selecting Arcadia Planitia as the ideal location for the Landing Zone and future base settlement.
    • Analyzed NASA datasets to confirm site viability across terrain relief, geothermal spots, subsurface ice (water resources), and radiation risks.
    • Designed a dual-mode platform (EVA/Rover) with vital-sign and navigation interfaces for astronaut AR helmets, forearm tablets, and rover consoles.
    • Started on Google Sites and migrated to Netlify to bypass code restrictions, achieving full offline capability and true GPS reliance.
    • Co-developed and refined the code with AI to integrate resource/hazard databases, warning alerts, and real-time waypoint creation.
    • Launched a scalable, offline-ready mapping app to secure astronaut survival from the LZ to the camp and beyond.
